body.resource_hint: On one nonzero positive-frequency test packet, factor out w(f,f)>0. The public species Gram is G=[[0,1],[1,0]], with eigenvectors (1,1) and (1,-1) of signs plus and minus. Hence it is not a positive Wightman matrix for two individually Hermitian fields. With kappa=G, the auxiliary Hilbert Gram G kappa is I, but the Hilbert adjoint is A*=kappa A^sharp kappa, so Omega*=Upsilon, T*=T and X*=-X. A Krein-selfadjoint A is Hilbert-selfadjoint iff kappa A kappa=A. For B=I and the negative-charge Q=E21, Q^sharp=Q, Q^2=0 and tr(B^sharp Q)=0, but ||Q||_HS^2=1: tr[(B+Q)^sharp(B+Q)]=2 while tr[(B+Q)^*(B+Q)]=3. Thus the auxiliary positive topology does not silently replace the generalized Born rule.
